name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
description: Adversaries abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution, often with encoding/obfuscation to evade detection.

name: User Execution: Malicious File
description: A user opens a malicious file delivered via email or download, resulting in execution of adversary code.

name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or password hashes are obtained.

name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
description: Adversaries communicate using application-layer protocols like HTTP/HTTPS to blend with legitimate traffic.

name: Application Layer Protocol
description: Adversaries communicate using application layer protocols to avoid detection/network filtering.

name: Phishing: Spearphishing Link
description: Adversaries send phishing emails containing a link to a credential-harvesting or malicious page.

name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
description: Adversaries dump credentials from the memory of the LSASS process, commonly via a memory dump technique.

name: Windows Management Instrumentation
description: Adversaries abuse WMI to execute malicious commands and payloads, often for lateral movement.

name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
description: Adversaries use valid accounts to interact with remote systems via SMB/admin shares for lateral movement.

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
description: Adversaries transfer tools or files from an external system into the compromised environment.

name: Account Discovery: Local Account
description: Adversaries enumerate local accounts on a system as part of discovery activity, often after gaining a foothold.

name: Dynamic Resolution
description: Adversaries dynamically establish connections using newly-registered or algorithmically generated domains to evade static blocklists.
